mainTopic: משה's trumpets, the materials of the מנורה, and the מנורה's measurements and decorations
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא: every כלי that משה made stayed valid for later generations, except the חצוצרות. To find out why, it looks at the word 'לך'. That word alone cannot be the reason, since the ארון also says 'לך'. The answer is that the trumpets have 'לך' written twice. Next comes a ברייתא about what the מנורה may be made from. רב פפא and רב יוסף disagree about what רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue over: cheap metals, or wood. רב יוסף proves from two more ברייתות that any metal is fine and only wood is disputed. Along the way we learn that one may not copy the מקדש's seven-branched מנורה. Then שמואל, quoting an elder, gives the מנורה's full blueprint: 18 טפחים tall, with 22 גביעים, 11 כפתורים and 9 פרחים, all of them required. The גמרא begins checking these numbers against the פסוקים, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משה's vessels stay valid, but not the trumpets
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: every כלי that משה made is valid for later generations, except the חצוצרות, which were valid only in his own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the vessels that משה made were valid for him and valid for future generations. But the trumpets were valid for him and invalid for future generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that started just before this text. It sets up a rule and one exception, the trumpets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that what משה made in the מדבר stays usable later. The trumpets are the one exception, and that exception is what the next steps will try to explain.

phrases.english: that Moshe made
are valid for him and valid for future generations.
The trumpets were valid for him
but invalid for future generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁעָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה, כְּשֵׁרִים לוֹ וּכְשֵׁרִים לְדוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of משה's כלים are valid for later generations, except the חצוצרות.

steps.title: Why were the trumpets different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source or reason that the חצוצרות were not valid for later generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The trumpets: what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the trumpets are the exception. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every other כלי of משה stays valid, the trumpets need a special reason. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק or logic creates that exception.

phrases.english: The trumpets: what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the exception stated in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that limits the חצוצרות to משה's time.

steps.title: 'For you' cannot mean 'only you', because the Ark also says it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'עשה לך' means 'for you and not for later generations'. It rejects this, because the ארון also says 'ועשית לך', and the ארון was valid for later generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because the verse says 'Make for you', meaning for you and not for future generations, then by that logic 'And make for you an Ark of wood' should also mean for you and not for future generations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason, the word 'לך', and right away attacks it using the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לך' alone meant 'only for משה', then the ארון would also be limited to his time. That contradicts the ברייתא, which says all of משה's כלים stayed valid. So 'לך' alone cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
if so, then (introduces an absurd result)

phrases.english: If you say it is because the verse says: 'Make for you'
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:2

phrases.english: for you, and not for future generations,
then by that logic, 'And make for you an Ark of wood'
phrases.notes: דברים 10:1

phrases.english: would that also mean for you and not for future generations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the word 'לך' limits the trumpets to משה's time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears for the ארון, which was valid for later generations, so the word cannot mean 'only for you'.

steps.title: The 'for you' of the trumpets may teach something else
steps.stepSummary: For the ארון, 'לך' must mean 'from your own money' or 'I prefer yours'. So the 'לך' of the trumpets could also be used for that, and it would not teach that they were temporary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, either according to the one who says 'for you' means 'from your own property', or according to the one who says 'As it were, I want yours more than theirs', this word here also is needed for that.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge continues. The 'לך' of the ארון is explained as teaching something else, so the 'לך' of the trumpets may also teach that same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two opinions about the meaning of 'לך' by the ארון: either משה must pay for it himself, or ה׳ especially wants משה's contribution. If 'לך' carries that meaning, then the trumpets' 'לך' is already used up for that, and nothing is left to show they were temporary.

keyTerms.meaning: as it were (said when speaking about ה׳)
it is needed for that teaching
according to the one who holds

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the answer yet. The word אלא here does not bring a solution. It explains the ארון and makes the question on the trumpets even stronger.

phrases.english: Rather, either according to the one who says:
'for you' means from your own property,
or according to the one who says:
'As it were, I want yours'
phrases.notes: ה׳ is speaking to משה: he prefers that משה himself provide it.

phrases.english: more than theirs,
this one too is needed for that teaching.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the 'לך' written by the trumpets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge from step 3 by giving the ארון's 'לך' another meaning and applying it to the trumpets.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'לך' as the source for the trumpets being temporary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'לך' by the ארון teaches 'from your own', then the same word by the trumpets is needed for that too, and cannot teach 'not for later generations'.

steps.title: The trumpets say 'for you' twice
steps.stepSummary: The trumpets are different because the פסוק says 'לך' two times. One is used for the regular teaching and the extra one teaches that they were only for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says 'for you' twice: 'Make for you' and 'they shall be for you'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The trumpets have an extra 'לך', and that extra word is the source for their being limited to משה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון has only one 'לך', and it is used for 'from your own'. The trumpets have two. The second one is free to teach that the trumpets were not valid for later generations.
steps.whatToRemember: משה's trumpets were only for his time because במדבר 10:2 says 'לך' twice ('עשה לך' and 'והיו לך'). One 'לך' alone would not be enough.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the trumpets.

phrases.english: because the verse says 'for you', 'for you', two times:
'Make for you' and 'they shall be for you'.
phrases.notes: Both are in במדבר 10:2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by counting the words in the פסוק (an extra word is free for another teaching).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'לך' by the ארון teaches 'from your own', the trumpets' 'לך' gives no source that they were temporary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The trumpets have two mentions of 'לך'. The extra one teaches they were valid only for משה, not for later generations.

steps.title: Which materials are valid for the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the מנורה should be made from one block of gold. Silver is valid. Cheaper metals are disputed between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Wood, bone and glass are invalid according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בריה דרב חנין taught before רב יוסף: The מנורה would come from a solid block of gold. If one made it of silver, it is valid. If of tin, lead or other metals, רבי invalidates it and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה validates it. If of wood, bone or glass, all agree it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about what materials the מנורה may be made from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. Gold is the ideal and silver is still valid. Lesser metals like tin and lead are disputed. Wood, bone and glass are not metal at all, and everyone agrees they are invalid.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up בַּעַץ (tin, a metal) with עֵץ (wood). Tin is disputed, but wood is invalid according to everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא opens the discussion of the מנורה's materials. In the next steps רב יוסף asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת, and both sides are traced back to how they read שמות 25:31.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חָנִין
phrases.english: Rav Pappa son of Rav Chanin taught
before Rav Yosef:
The Menorah would be made
from a solid block, from gold.
If one made it of silver, it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל בַּעַץ וְשֶׁל אֲבָר וְשֶׁל גִּיסְטְרוֹן –
phrases.english: If of tin, or of lead, or of other metals:
phrases.notes: בַּעַץ here means tin, not wood. Wood (עֵץ) comes up a few words later.

phrases.english: Rebbi rules it invalid
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda rules it valid.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל עֵץ וְשֶׁל עֶצֶם וְשֶׁל זְכוּכִית –
phrases.english: If of wood, or of bone, or of glass:
everyone agrees it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חָנִין קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the materials of the מנורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gold מנורה is ideal and silver is valid. Tin, lead and other metals are disputed (רבי invalid, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה valid). Wood, bone and glass are invalid according to everyone.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks how the dispute should be understood
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רב פפא בריה דרב חנין to explain the reasoning behind the מחלוקת between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is your view?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks his colleague to explain what the two תנאים in the ברייתא about the מנורה are really arguing about. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 6 gave the rulings but not the reasons. Now the גמרא looks for the logic underneath the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your opinion? How do you understand it?

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your opinion?
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is the one asking, and he is talking to רב פפא בריה דרב חנין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind the מחלוקת of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about the materials of the מנורה.

steps.title: Both use generalizations and details but read the detail differently
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that both תנאים use כללי ופרטי. One says the detail (gold) teaches 'any metal,' and the other says it teaches 'anything valuable.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Both of them learn through generalizations and details. But one holds: just as the detail is clearly a metal, so too anything made of metal. And the other holds: just as the detail is clearly something valuable, so too anything valuable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains that the two תנאים use the same method of reading the פסוק. They only disagree about which quality of gold is the one that matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With כלל ופרט, you include things that are similar to the detail. Gold has two qualities: it is a metal, and it is valuable. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה focuses on 'metal,' so even cheap metals are fine. רבי focuses on 'valuable,' so cheap metals are not.

keyTerms.meaning: Generalizations and details, a method of learning from the wording of a פסוק
The detail that the פסוק spells out (here: gold)
'The master'; here it refers to one of the תנאים

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּין מָר וּבֵין מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Both this Sage and that Sage
interpret using generalizations and details.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is שמות 25:31, about making the מנורה from pure gold.

phrases.english: But one Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

phrases.english: just as the stated detail is a type of metal,
so too anything made of metal,
and the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי.

phrases.english: just as the stated detail is something valuable,
so too anything valuable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין מָר וּבֵין מָר כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי דָּרְשִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both use כלל ופרט. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה includes anything metal, and רבי includes only valuable things.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a different version where the dispute is about wood
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells רב פפא to set aside his ברייתא in favor of another one. In that ברייתא, רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue about כלי שרת made of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Put your ברייתא aside in favor of mine. For it was taught: Temple vessels that were made of wood — רבי says they are invalid, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on רב פפא by quoting a different ברייתא. In it, the two תנאים argue about wood, not about cheap metals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, no one would ever allow wood, because wood is neither a metal nor valuable. But רב יוסף's ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does allow wood. So רב פפא's explanation cannot fit this version, and a new explanation will be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove your source in favor of mine
Vessels used for the service in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In step 6, everyone agrees that wood is invalid. In רב יוסף's ברייתא, wood is exactly what רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue about.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סְמִי דִּידָךְ מִקַּמֵּי דִּידִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: Remove yours in light of mine.
phrases.notes: Literally 'remove yours before mine.' He means: don't rely on your ברייתא, rely on mine.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן שֶׁל עֵץ,
phrases.english: As it is taught: Service vessels that one made of wood,
רבי deems them unfit,
and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה deems them fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ברייתא that רב פפא was explaining and brings a different version of the מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation, which is based on the ברייתא in step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב יוסף's ברייתא, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows wood. A rule of 'any metal' or 'anything valuable' could never include wood.

steps.title: The dispute is about which method of reading to use
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רבי reads the פסוק with כללי ופרטי, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads it with ריבויי ומיעוטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree? רבי learns through generalizations and details, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns through inclusions and exclusions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains what is behind the מחלוקת in his ברייתא. The two תנאים use different methods for reading the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is different from רב פפא's view, where both used the same method. Here the disagreement is about the method itself. כלל ופרט stays close to the detail, while ריבוי ומיעוט includes much more, so it can even include wood.

keyTerms.meaning: Inclusions and exclusions, a broader method of reading a פסוק
Interprets, learns out from the פסוק

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
רבי interprets using generalizations and details,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי.
phrases.english: and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה interprets using amplifications and restrictions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב יוסף's ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about the method: כללי ופרטי versus ריבויי ומיעוטי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same פסוק can lead to different rulings, depending on which method of reading is used.

steps.title: רבי's reading: generalization, detail, generalization teaches 'metal'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף shows how רבי reads the פסוק as a כלל ופרט וכלל: 'make a מנורה' (general), 'pure gold' (detail), 'of beaten work shall the מנורה be made' (general again). The result is that any metal is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי learns through generalizations and details: 'And you shall make a מנורה' is a generalization. 'Pure gold' is a detail. 'Of beaten work shall the מנורה be made' is a generalization again. A generalization, a detail and a generalization: you include only things similar to the detail. Just as the detail is clearly a metal, so too anything made of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף goes through the פסוק word by word to show how רבי's method works. The conclusion is that the מנורה may be made from any metal, but not from wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With כלל ופרט וכלל, you include only things that are like the detail. Here the shared quality is metal. So רבי excludes wood, which matches his ruling in רב יוסף's ברייתא. Notice that in רב יוסף's version, it is רבי who allows any metal.

keyTerms.meaning: A generalization, then a detail, then another generalization
Hammered out from one solid piece

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף: רבי uses כלל ופרט, so any metal is allowed but wood is not. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses ריבוי ומיעוט, so even wood is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: In רב פפא's explanation, the 'any metal' view belonged to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. In רב יוסף's explanation, the 'any metal' view belongs to רבי.

phrases.english: רבי interprets using generalizations and details:
'And you shall make a Candelabrum' is a generalization,
phrases.notes: שמות 25:31. No material is mentioned yet, so it is general.

phrases.english: 'pure gold' is a detail,
'of beaten work shall the Candelabrum be made' — it generalized again,
a generalization, a detail and a generalization,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט:
phrases.english: you may only include what is similar to the detail:
just as the stated detail is a type of metal,
so too anything made of metal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דָּרֵישׁ כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי, וְעָשִׂיתָ מְנֹרַת כָּלַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out רבי's side of the explanation given in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading the פסוק as כלל ופרט וכלל teaches that any metal is valid, so wood is invalid.

steps.title: How רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads the פסוק as include, exclude, include
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses ריבויי ומיעוטי. 'Make a מנורה' includes, 'pure gold' excludes, and 'beaten work' includes again. So everything is included except earthenware.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns using 'include and exclude.' 'And you shall make a מנורה' includes. 'Pure gold' excludes. 'Of beaten work shall the מנורה be made' includes again. When the פסוק includes, excludes and includes again, it includes everything. What does it include? All materials. What does it exclude? Earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his explanation by showing how רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads the same פסוק in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ריבויי ומיעוטי, the middle 'exclusion' takes out very little. Only the material furthest from gold, earthenware, is excluded. That is why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows even wood, while רבי (step 11) allowed only metals.

keyTerms.meaning: A way of reading פסוקים based on 'including' and 'excluding' words
Include, exclude, include again: everything is included except the one most unlike the exclusion
Beaten or hammered out of one piece

steps.whatToRemember: רבי, using כלל ופרט וכלל, allows any metal. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, using ריבוי ומיעוט וריבוי, allows anything, even wood, except earthenware.
steps.confusionAlert: It is the same פסוק and the same three phrases as in step 11. Only the reading method is different, and that changes how much is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda interprets with inclusions and exclusions:
'And you shall make a candelabrum' – it included,
phrases.notes: שמות 25:31

phrases.english: 'pure gold' – it excluded,
'of beaten work shall the candelabrum be made' – it went back and included.
It included, excluded, and included – it included everything,
and what did it include? It included all things,
and what did it exclude? It excluded one of earthenware.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of רב יוסף's explanation, after רבי's reading in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads ריבה ומיעט וריבה, so all materials are included except earthenware.

steps.title: רב פפא says the opposite: drop your ברייתא for mine
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא turns רב יוסף's words back on him. Set aside your ברייתא because of mine.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Remove your ברייתא in favor of mine!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back. He says there is no reason his ברייתא should be the one dropped, so maybe רב יוסף's should be dropped instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רב יוסף told רב פפא to set aside his ברייתא, the one where the argument is about metals. Now רב פפא throws the same demand back. This forces רב יוסף to prove why his version is the right one.

keyTerms.meaning: Yours / mine (here, your ברייתא / my ברייתא)

phrases.english: On the contrary, remove yours in the face of mine!
phrases.notes: The text doesn't say who is speaking, but it is רב פפא answering רב יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's demand from step 9 by turning it around.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that his ברייתא should be preferred
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing shows that רב יוסף's ברייתא is more reliable, so you could just as easily drop his and keep רב פפא's.

steps.title: First proof: another ברייתא where the only argument is about wood
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא. Without gold, one may use silver, copper, iron, tin or lead, and only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: That can't enter your mind, because it was taught: If he has no gold, he may bring even one of silver, copper, iron, tin or lead. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows even one of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects רב פפא's idea and supports his own version with another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, the first opinion (רבי) already allows all metals. The only argument is about wood. This matches רב יוסף's version, not רב פפא's, where the argument was about metals.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't even think it; that idea is impossible

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ זָהָב מֵבִיא אַף שֶׁל כֶּסֶף,
phrases.english: If he has no gold, he brings even one of silver,
of copper, of iron,
and of tin, and of lead.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר אַף בְּשֶׁל עֵץ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit even of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף answers רב פפא's challenge with outside support.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי allows all metals and the מחלוקת is only about wood
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the allowed metals, where only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds wood

steps.title: Second proof: no copying the מקדש, not even a seven-branched מנורה of other metals
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא forbids copying the היכל, אולם, עזרה, שלחן and מנורה. A seven-branched מנורה may not be made even from other metals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: A person may not build a house shaped like the היכל, a porch like the אולם, a courtyard like the עזרה, a table like the שלחן, or a מנורה like the מנורה. But he may make one with five, six or eight branches. He may not make one with seven, even from other kinds of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings another ברייתא that also shows other metals are fine for the real מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is forbidden to copy something that is fit for the מקדש. Since even a seven-branched מנורה of other metals may not be made, that tells us a metal מנורה would be valid in the מקדש. So the חכמים allow all metals, just as רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: The main building of the מקדש
The entrance hall of the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is also the source for the well-known הלכה that one may not make a seven-branched מנורה like the one in the מקדש.

phrases.english: And it is taught in another one:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בַּיִת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל,
phrases.english: A person may not make a house in the form of the Sanctuary,
a portico corresponding to the Entrance Hall,
a courtyard corresponding to the Temple courtyard,
a table corresponding to the Table,
a candelabrum corresponding to the Candelabrum,
but he may make one of five
phrases.notes: He means five branches.

phrases.english: and of six and of eight,
but of seven he may not make,
even from other kinds of metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא supporting the same point as step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנורה of other metals is valid for the מקדש according to the חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ban on copying a seven-branched מנורה even from other metals

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: not even a wooden copy, like the חשמונאים made
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה forbids even a wooden copy, because the חשמונאי kings made one of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: He may not make one even of wood, the way the kings of the חשמונאי family made it.
steps.whatsHappening: The second ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's opinion. This sets up the חכמים' answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He forbids a wooden copy because he holds that a wooden מנורה is valid in the מקדש. This fits his view in step 14. His proof is that the חשמונאים used a wooden מנורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The kings of the Hasmonean family

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
He may not make one even of wood,
in the way that the kings of the Hasmonean house made it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף שֶׁל עֵץ לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, giving the opposing opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a wooden seven-branched מנורה may not be made, since a wooden one was used in the מקדש by the חשמונאים.

steps.title: The חכמים: the חשמונאים' מנורה was iron, not wood
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof. It was made of iron spits covered with tin, and later of silver and then gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that your proof? They were iron spits, and they covered them with tin. When they became richer, they made it of silver. When they became richer again, they made it of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים knock down רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's proof from the חשמונאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חשמונאים never used wood. They used cheap metal, iron, and upgraded as they could afford it. So the story only supports other metals, which the חכמים already allow, and not wood.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (said to reject it)

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות show that everyone allows a מנורה of any metal. The only argument between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is about wood, which supports רב יוסף's version.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there a proof from there?

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפּוּדִים שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל הָיוּ, וְחִיפּוּם בְּבַעַץ.
phrases.english: They were spits of iron, and they covered them with tin.
When they grew rich, they made them of silver,
when they again grew rich, they made them of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the historical proof given in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the חשמונאים, not רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The facts are wrong: the חשמונאים' מנורה was iron covered with tin, not wood.

steps.title: The height of the מנורה and its lower section
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, quoting an elder, says the מנורה is eighteen טפחים tall. He then maps the bottom nine טפחים of the center shaft.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said in the name of an elder: The מנורה is eighteen טפחים tall. The feet and the flower on them take up three טפחים. Then come two plain טפחים. Then one טפח with a cup, a knob and a flower. Then two more plain טפחים. Then one טפח with a knob.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new piece: a blueprint of the מנורה, built from the bottom up. This step covers the base and the lower part of the middle shaft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far: 3 (base and flower) + 2 (plain) + 1 (cup, knob, flower) + 2 (plain) + 1 (knob) = 9 טפחים. That last knob is where the first pair of branches will come out, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: The candelabrum in the בית המקדש
A handbreadth, a unit of measurement
Smooth or plain, with no decoration

phrases.english: Shmuel said in the name of an elder:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבְהָהּ שֶׁל מְנוֹרָה שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: The height of the Menorah is eighteen handbreadths.
The feet and the flower take up three handbreadths,
then two handbreadths are plain,
then one handbreadth that has a cup, a knob and a flower,
then two handbreadths plain, and one handbreadth with a knob.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier steps discussed what the מנורה may be made from. Now the גמרא turns to its exact shape and measurements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנורה is 18 טפחים tall, and its first 9 טפחים are laid out in a fixed order of plain and decorated sections.

steps.title: The three pairs of branches and the top of the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: Out of each of three knobs, a pair of branches comes out and rises to the full height. Plain sections separate them, and the top three טפחים hold three cups, a knob and a flower.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two branches come out of that knob, one to each side, and they rise up to the height of the מנורה. Then one טפח is plain and one טפח has a knob, and two more branches come out of it, and they rise the same way. Then one plain טפח and one טפח with a knob, and two more branches come out of it and rise the same way. Then two plain טפחים. That leaves three טפחים, which hold three cups, a knob and a flower.
steps.whatsHappening: The elder continues the blueprint up the center shaft. Three pairs of branches come out, one pair from each knob, and then he describes the very top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair of branches comes out of a knob: at the 9th, 11th and 13th טפח. Then come 2 plain טפחים (reaching 15), and the last 3 טפחים bring the total to exactly 18. All six branches curve up to the same height as the middle shaft.

keyTerms.meaning: They stretch out and go up
There remained, there were left over

steps.confusionAlert: The text repeats almost the same lines three times. This is not a mistake. It describes three separate pairs of branches, one above the other.

phrases.english: And two branches come out of it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the knob just mentioned, at the end of the last step.

phrases.english: one going this way and one going that way,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְשָׁכִין וְעוֹלִין כְּנֶגֶד גּוֹבְהָהּ שֶׁל מְנוֹרָה,
phrases.english: and they stretch out and rise up to the height of the Menorah.
Then one handbreadth plain, and one handbreadth with a knob,
and two branches come out of it,
one going this way and one going that way,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְשָׁכִין וְעוֹלִין כְּנֶגֶד גּוֹבְהָהּ שֶׁל מְנוֹרָה,
phrases.english: stretching out and rising up to the height of the Menorah.
Then one handbreadth plain, and one handbreadth with a knob,
and two branches come out of it,
one going this way and one going that way,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְשָׁכִין וְעוֹלִין כְּנֶגֶד גּוֹבְהָהּ שֶׁל מְנוֹרָה,
phrases.english: and they stretch out and rise up to the height of the Menorah.
Then two handbreadths plain.
There remained three handbreadths,
which have three cups, a knob and a flower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same blueprint, from the 9th טפח up to the top.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three pairs of branches come out of three knobs. Plain sections separate them, and the top three טפחים have three cups, a knob and a flower.

steps.title: What the decorations look like and how many there are
steps.stepSummary: The elder describes the shape of the גביעים, כפתורים and פרחים. He then gives the totals: 22 cups, 11 knobs and 9 flowers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do the cups look like? Like Alexandrian cups. What do the knobs look like? Like Cretan apples. What do the flowers look like? Like the flower designs on columns. In total there are twenty-two cups, eleven knobs and nine flowers.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know where the decorations go, the elder explains what each one looks like. Then he adds them all up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle shaft has 4 cups, 5 knobs and 3 flowers. Each of the six branches has 3 cups, a knob and a flower, which adds 18 cups, 6 knobs and 6 flowers. Together that makes 22 cups, 11 knobs and 9 flowers.

keyTerms.meaning: Cups in the style of Alexandria
Apples of the Cretans (a known kind of apple)
And it turns out that there are (a total)

phrases.english: And the cups, what do they look like?
Like Alexandrian cups.
The knobs, what do they look like?
Like the apples of the Cretans.
The flowers, what do they look like?
Like the flower designs on columns.
So there turn out to be twenty-two cups,
eleven knobs, and nine flowers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After placing the decorations, the elder now describes their shapes and adds them up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנורה has 22 גביעים, 11 כפתורים and 9 פרחים, each with a set shape.

steps.title: Every single decoration is required
steps.stepSummary: Each cup, knob and flower is required. If even one is missing, the whole מנורה is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The cups hold each other back. The knobs hold each other back. The flowers hold each other back. And the cups, knobs and flowers all hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The elder ends with the practical rule: the מנורה must have every one of its decorations. Missing even one ruins the whole thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעכבין זה את זה means that each part is necessary for the others to count. This applies within each type (all 22 cups are needed) and across the types (cups, knobs and flowers all depend on each other). So a מנורה with 21 cups, or with no flowers, is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold back: each one is required, so missing it makes the item invalid
Cups, knobs and flowers, all three types together

steps.whatToRemember: The מנורה is 18 טפחים tall with 22 גביעים, 11 כפתורים and 9 פרחים. Every single one is required: missing any decoration makes the מנורה not valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the blueprint to a real law. The decorations are not just for beauty; they are part of what makes it a kosher מנורה.

phrases.english: The cups hold each other back,
phrases.notes: 'Hold back' means each one is required: if one is missing, the others don't count either.

phrases.english: the knobs hold each other back,
the flowers hold each other back,
and the cups, knobs and flowers
hold each other back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing and counting the decorations, the elder gives the law that all of them are required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every גביע, כפתור and פרח is required, both within each type and across all three types.

steps.title: Granted, the 22 cups come straight from the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the number of cups fits the פסוקים: four on the center shaft, and three on each branch. This prepares a question about the knobs and flowers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that there are twenty-two cups. One פסוק says the מנורה itself has four cups. Another פסוק says each branch has three almond-shaped cups with a knob and a flower. So there are four cups on the center shaft...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question. It says the elder's count of 22 cups is easy to understand from the פסוקים, which hints that some other number from the elder's list will be harder to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'it makes sense that...' and usually comes before a 'but' question. Here the גמרא builds the 22 from two פסוקים: 4 cups on the center shaft, plus 3 cups on each of the six branches. This section ends after the first part of that math, the 4 cups of the center shaft.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (opens a 'this part is fine, but...' question)
Its own (belonging to the מנורה's center shaft)

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא does not mean the גמרא is finished. It means 'this part works.' A question about a different part is coming next.

phrases.english: It makes sense that there are twenty-two cups,
as it is written: "And in the מנורה four cups, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 25:34

phrases.english: and it is written: "Three almond-shaped cups
on the one branch, a knob and a flower, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 25:33. The rest of this פסוק applies the same pattern to all six branches.

phrases.english: so there are four cups of its own
phrases.notes: He means the four cups on the center shaft. The count continues in the next part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the elder's totals from step 20 and begins checking them against the פסוקים, starting with the 22 cups.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוקים support each of the elder's totals. The cups are accepted here, and a question on the other numbers is being prepared.
steps.kashyaTarget: The elder's totals in step 20, which the גמרא is checking against the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 22 cups fit the פסוקים (4 on the center shaft plus 3 on each of the six branches). This 'granted' part sets up a challenge to another of the elder's numbers, which does not come out as easily from the פסוקים.
